messages:
sasha: Heads-up — CI on main flipped red right after the midnight deploy. Failing step is secrets-decrypt in gha-runner, looks permission-related.
ci-bot: [AUTOMATION] workflow 'integration-tests' failed on commit abc123 (exit 1) — see logs: https://ci.internal/reports/abc123 :warning:
rahul: I can take a look, tagging @jamie in case we need a bisect. Any recent creds rotation?
sasha: Not from infra side, last KMS rotation was last month. We did rotate a GitHub App token two days ago for a subset of repos, could be fallout.
jamie: Oof, that apps-token rotate touched the deploy payloads. Can you paste the exact job log snippet?
sasha: Sure — from the runner: ```Error: KMS.Decrypt denied: iam.permissionDenied for serviceAccount-ci@example.com
	at /runner/actions/decrypt.js:42:14```
olivia: That stack looks like the runner SA lost access to the KMS key in the target repo's project. I saw an automated policy change yesterday (org-pol:restrict-service-accounts). Might be related.
rahul: TL;DR: repo secret provider can't read key. Quick tests: 1) does the runner SA still have roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on the key? 2) is the key still mapped in vault->repo sync?
jamie: I'll try a hotfix — re-add the decrypter role and re-run the job. If that fixes it we can roll a scoped policy exception.
sasha: Please do. If re-add works, we should then audit the repo binding propagation; there might be a timing issue in the policy webhook.
ci-bot: [ACTION] re-run requested by jamie — queued (run #4578).
jamie: Rebind applied: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/pX/locations/global/keyR --member=serviceAccount:service-account-ci@... --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`
jamie: Re-run started.
ci-bot: [AUTOMATION] run #4578 started.
ci-bot: [AUTOMATION] run #4578 failed at secrets-decrypt step (same error).
rahul: Hmm same error after rebind — either wrong key or the runner is using a cached credential that got revoked. Can someone check the GH App installation token expiry and the runner token lease?
olivia: Checking logs — runner shows `token lease expired` 12:03 UTC. The autoscaled runner image refresh didn't pick up new app token.
jamie: Ok increment plan: 1) force restart self-hosted runners in the pool, 2) rotate the app installation token again with a new secret sync, 3) if still failing, bisect the recent org policy change.
sasha: I'm on restart now. Small ask: @rahul can you prepare a simple bisect checklist if this persists?
rahul: Will do — items: snapshot failing commit, verify key binding, check app-token TTL, check vault sync, run local decrypt test with `gcloud kms decrypt --ciphertext-file` as `service-account-ci`.
ci-bot: [AUTOMATION] runner pool restart requested by sasha.
jamie: Restart finished, re-run queued.
ci-bot: [AUTOMATION] run #4580 started.
ci-bot: [AUTOMATION] run #4580 SUCCESS — all steps passed :tada:
sasha: Nice — looks like runner restart picked up fresh tokens. Thanks all.
olivia: Follow-up: I'll open a short RFC for making runner token refresh explicit during app-token rotations and add a short postmortem link when I have it.
rahul: And I'll add a smoke test to the secret-sync job to catch KMS decrypt failures earlier.
jamie: Leaving a :thumbsup: — will watch the RFC and help on rollout.
sasha: Closing the loop here — if anyone sees re-occurrence ping this thread. Thanks!
